title: PGC Invariant Schema V0
description: Closed machine-block contract for INVARIANT artifacts. Every accepted field has a semantic consumer or a compile-time validation role; explanatory material lives below the Machine fence.

governed_by.description: FQDN of the governing constitution. Source of the GOVERNED_BY edge.

enforcement_stage.description: Invariant class discriminator (rule_ownership.md). compiler_* stages are evaluated by an ASSERT handler in S4; runtime_outcome is enforced by a CC violation outcome and WF routing, and verified by ASSERT_RUNTIME_INVARIANT_WIRED_V0; composition_conformance is evaluated by the assembler's Composition Conformance phase over the assembled snapshot. Each stage names the mechanism that enforces the invariant, and an invariant enforced by a non-compiler mechanism has no same-named ASSERT — a compile-time handler could only evaluate one domain build, which is precisely the scope a composition-scoped rule is not about. Two further stages carry an obligation the build does not: enforced_elsewhere names a mechanism outside the build and requires core.enforced_by to say which, and declared_not_enforced states that the obligation is stated deliberately and carried by nothing yet. The second exists because an obligation deferred and never built is otherwise indistinguishable from one in force — fourteen of eighty-seven checks on this platform have no path that produces a refusal, and ten say so only in prose nothing reads.

violation_response.description: Paired discriminator. BUSINESS_VIOLATION is admissible only for runtime_outcome invariants.

runtime_binding.description: Required for runtime_outcome invariants, forbidden otherwise. Proven against the CC result surface and WF routing by ASSERT_RUNTIME_INVARIANT_WIRED_V0.

enforced_by.description: The mechanism carrying this obligation where the build does not. Required when enforcement_stage names a stage that routes the obligation elsewhere, refused otherwise. A delegation nobody can follow is indistinguishable from an absence, and absence is not permission.

assert_projection.description: Parameters carried into the ASSERT descriptor derived from this invariant (S4 _derive_assert). Read by the bound handler via current_assert_artifact. scope.applies_to is the single declared authority for invariant applicability; domain vs platform is derived from it by kind intersection, never declared.

applies_to_kinds.description: The artifact kinds this invariant governs. Authoritative for governance import: an invariant is domain-applicable iff this intersects the domain-instantiated kind set. Distinct axis from scope.applies_to (which is layer/surface).

handler.description: Handler module override. Omitted means convention: <prefix>.<assert_code lowercased>.

scope.description: Layer/surface an invariant governs (PLATFORM, or a domain layer code). Read by surface-scoped handlers (e.g. surface closure) to filter artifacts by layer, and by the import filter: a layer-scoped invariant is surface-specific and NOT generically imported into domain builds — each surface declares its own. Optional; present only where a handler needs it. This is a distinct axis from applies_to_kinds.

composition_check.description: Declarative specification for evaluating this invariant against an assembled composition (Composition Conformance phase). Encoding- and language-neutral: a selector over canonical artifacts plus a cardinality rule. Present iff the invariant is composition-scoped; its presence is what admits the invariant into the phase. Carries no implementation reference.

rule.description: Cardinality rule the selected artifact set must satisfy.

selector.description: Predicate selecting canonical artifacts from the assembled snapshot. All declared fields must match (logical AND). An empty selector is invalid.

namespace.description: Exact match on the artifact's namespace.

artifact_type.description: Exact match on the artifact's compiled type token.

artifact_code_prefix.description: Artifact code must start with this string.

where.description: Exact-match constraints on the artifact's declaration fields. A key may be a dotted path into nested declarations (e.g. handler.kind); a single segment is a top-level field.

subject.description: Human-readable name of what is being constrained, used in diagnostics.

fqdn.description: Authoritative declared identity (namespace::code). Folder location has no authority over identity.

supersedes.description: FQDN of the artifact this one stands in place of. A declared relation between two exact identities, not a resolution rule: references stay exact, and a superseded artifact is unreachable rather than absent.

superseded_by.description: FQDNs of the artifacts that stand in this one's place. Several is the ordinary case — one act split in two retires one artifact and authors two. Its presence means the artifact is superseded: unreachable from the executable projections, retained in the canonical set as history.

authority.description: The authority from which this artifact's jurisdiction derives (CA-1, CA-2). Declared, never inferred from namespace, path or kind.

concern.description: The semantic subject this artifact is about (GO-11, ID-12). A concern classification confers no authority and constitutes no boundary.
